messages.subject: plot R3 to S2
parts:
Hi All,

I have a set of LAT-LONG and utilizing a methodology similar to the Blangiardo spde spatial model, with the hope of progressing to a spatio-temporal model.

As far as what I have read in the papers and the discussion group I have two options

1) Convert lat-long to UMTX and UMTY
2) Convert lat-long to 3d Cartesian XYZ

It seems that you favor method 2 so that is what I am sticking with. I was hoping you could give me ideas how to plot the mesh resulting from my R3 specification to check that my borders etc are correct.

Thanks for any assistance

Sam

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] plot R3 to S2
parts:
Which model domain is preferred for geographical coordinates depends
on the size of the domain. If the region is small enough, UMTX/UTMY
should be fine, but if the domain is large enough to "notice" the
curvature of the globe, using the sphere itself (or a subset) gives
correct distances.

To plot spherical fields (or part-spherical in your case, as far as I
understand), the same inla.mesh.project/or methods can be used as for
planar meshes. The documentation for that has unfortunately lagged
behind a bit...

Available projections is sphere-->long&lat-grid (projection="longlat),
sphere-->long&sin(lat) (projection="longsinlat"; this is an equal-area
projection), the mollweide projection (projection="mollweide"; this is
also equal are, but with less shape distortion), and also any
projection defined by points of your own choosing, such as a grid in
UMTX/Y (which you first have to project onto XYZ on the sphere).

You can also produce a 3d-plot use rgl using some old functionality.
Off the top off my head, I think
plot(old.mesh.class(mesh),col=somevalues)
should do the trick.

/Finn
